items.text:
Recommended MoSCoW for every FR and NFR, by domain (FR-005, FR-011, FR-031 and FR-032 are decided in their own questions):

| Domain | ID | Title | Recommended |
|---|---|---|---|
| sections | FR-001 | Show the hero with name, role and primary call to action | must |
| sections | FR-004 | Show the proof strip of key numbers and facts | must |
| sections | FR-006 | Show selected work as anonymized glass cards | must |
| sections | FR-008 | Show the How I can help offer | must |
| sections | FR-009 | State the pre-sales result line | must |
| sections | FR-010 | Show the experience timeline | must |
| sections | FR-012 | List certifications and speaking | must |
| sections | FR-013 | Show Champion status with the official badge when available | must |
| sections | FR-014 | Show a placeholder portrait with a swappable photo slot | must |
| motion | FR-002 | Play the opening sequence - the last boring homepage (Act 1) | must |
| motion | FR-003 | Turn the drifting constellation into a governed graph on scroll (Act 2) | must |
| motion | FR-007 | Slide work cards in along the graph and highlight their part of it (Act 4) | should |
| motion | FR-016 | Settle the page at contact (Act 6) | should |
| motion | FR-017 | Deep-link to a chapter in its final state | should |
| motion | FR-018 | Drift the constellation with scroll and pointer | should |
| motion | FR-019 | Reveal each section as it enters the viewport | should |
| contact | FR-015 | Contact Jakub by email, LinkedIn or GitHub | must |
| footer | FR-020 | Show the How this site was built note | must |
| footer | FR-021 | Show the legal entity and privacy note in the footer | must |
| content | FR-022 | Update all page content from one content file | must |
| content | FR-023 | Reserve a flagged-off How I deliver section | must |
| content | FR-030 | Reserve a flagged-off testimonial slot | could |
| content | NFR-025 | Plain hyphen only, never em or en dashes, in copy and code comments | must |
| content | NFR-026 | The brand is the person - JacOps only as the footer legal entity | must |
| seo | FR-024 | Produce a proper link preview card | must |
| delivery | FR-025 | Publish site changes on merge to main | must |
| cv | FR-026 | Download the CV as a PDF | should |
| theming | FR-027 | Follow the system light or dark theme | should |
| hosting | FR-028 | Show a custom 404 page | should |
| hosting | FR-029 | Redirect www to the apex domain | should |
| performance | NFR-001 | Lighthouse 95+ and LCP under 2.5 s on a mid-range phone | must |
| performance | NFR-002 | Animation never blocks reading - hero text is the first-frame LCP element | must |
| performance | NFR-006 | Automatic reduced variant on low-power devices | should |
| performance | NFR-007 | No endless animation - motion rests and pauses when not visible | should |
| performance | NFR-010 | Rendering stack - CSS 3D plus Canvas 2D or SVG, WebGL only lazy and proven | should |
| accessibility | NFR-003 | WCAG 2.2 AA, including contrast over the animated background in both themes | must |
| accessibility | NFR-004 | Full content readable with JavaScript off | must |
| accessibility | NFR-005 | Reduced-motion variant honours prefers-reduced-motion | must |
| ux | NFR-008 | Native scrolling - no scroll hijacking or scroll traps | must |
| ux | NFR-009 | Shared motion tokens and input-appropriate motion | should |
| ux | NFR-011 | Responsive from 360 px with mobile as a first-class layout | must |
| ux | NFR-029 | Reads as a CV in 60 seconds | must |
| security | NFR-012 | HTTPS-only delivery from a private origin with security headers | must |
| security | NFR-013 | No long-lived cloud credentials - deploy via GitHub Actions OIDC | must |
| security | NFR-017 | No third-party origins at runtime | must |
| privacy-and-compliance | NFR-014 | Public repository hygiene - no secrets or private details | must |
| privacy-and-compliance | NFR-015 | Client anonymity and the traceability rule | must |
| privacy-and-compliance | NFR-016 | No cookies and no third-party trackers | must |

options: Keep all as listed
Change some (name the ids)
items.why: Brief Needs Must/Should/Could lists; unranked motion items set to should per Open decision 4

items.text: Needs (Must) 2 and 5 ask for the breakout figure (Act 3, FR-005) and a timeline line that draws with scroll (Act 5, FR-011), but Open decision 4 says Acts 3 to 6 may ship as plain reveals if the budget is tight. Which rule sets their priority?
options: Must - both ship as described whatever the budget
Should - both ship if the motion budget allows, else plain reveals
items.recommended: Should - both ship if the motion budget allows, else plain reveals
items.why: Brief Open decision 4 is the later, specific rule; keeps the MVP from widening

quotes.text: One figure "breaks out of its frame" (see Act 3).
Acts 3 to 6 can ship as plain reveals if the budget is tight

items.answer: Should - both ship if the motion budget allows, else plain reveals

items.text: No uptime target exists, and only the DNS cut-over has a rollback (NFR-022). What uptime should the site hold, and how is a bad release undone?
options: 99.9% monthly; a bad release restored within 15 min from S3 versioning or per-release prefixes
99.5% monthly; a bad release undone by reverting the commit and redeploying within 1 h
Best effort, no target; fix forward
items.recommended: 99.5% monthly; a bad release undone by reverting the commit and redeploying within 1 h
items.why: Research - deploy finding: sync with delete removes the old build; content history already lives in git

rows.risk: No agreed bar for an outage on launch day, so nobody knows when one matters
A sync with delete removes the previous build, so a broken release has no quick way back

items.answer: 99.5% monthly; a bad release undone by reverting the commit and redeploying within 1 h

items.text: CloudFront access logs hold visitor IP addresses, which are personal data under GDPR, and nothing says whether they are kept. What happens to them?
options: CloudFront access logging off
Logging on, IPs kept 30 days then deleted, named in the privacy note
items.why: Research - GDPR access-log finding; keeps the NFR-016 no-tracking note true at no cost

rows.area: CDN access logs with IP addresses
rows.risk: Logs hold personal data and could make the no-tracking privacy note untrue

items.text: FR-024 asks for an Open Graph image but sets no size or source. LinkedIn wants at least 1200 x 627 px. Where does the image come from?
options: 1200 x 627 px, generated at build from the content file
1200 x 627 px, designed once and committed as a static file
items.recommended: 1200 x 627 px, generated at build from the content file
items.why: Research - link preview finding (1200 x 627, under 5 MB); NFR-023 single source of truth

steps: Launch post shares the jacops.pl link
LinkedIn shows the card with title, description and image
Months later Jakub edits the headline in the content file

outcomes.1200 x 627 px, generated at build from t: The card image shows the new headline after the next deploy
outcomes.1200 x 627 px, designed once and committ: The card image keeps the old headline until someone redraws it

items.answer: 1200 x 627 px, generated at build from the content file

items.text: Nothing tells Jakub when the site is down, a deploy fails or the bill grows. Which alerts should exist?
options: Budget alerts at 80% and 100% of 2 USD, email on a failed deploy, uptime check every 5 min with email
Budget alerts at 80% and 100% of 2 USD and email on a failed deploy; no uptime check
Email on a failed deploy only
items.recommended: Budget alerts at 80% and 100% of 2 USD and email on a failed deploy; no uptime check
items.why: Research - budget alert finding; a static site behind a CDN rarely goes down and a probe adds cost against NFR-019

rows.risk: A traffic spike or misconfiguration bills for days before anyone sees it
A content change silently never goes live
An outage during the launch post goes unnoticed

items.answer: Budget alerts at 80% and 100% of 2 USD and email on a failed deploy; no uptime check

items.text: FR-025 deploys on merge but says nothing about caching: a visitor mid-deploy can get old HTML with new assets. How soon must a merged change be live?
options: Within 10 min; the pipeline waits for the invalidation, hashed assets cached long, HTML short
Within 1 h through a short HTML cache, no invalidation
items.recommended: Within 10 min; the pipeline waits for the invalidation, hashed assets cached long, HTML short
items.why: Research - deploy cache finding (long TTL on hashed assets, short on HTML, awaited invalidation)

steps: CI builds, tests and uploads the new files
CloudFront still holds the old HTML in cache

outcomes.Within 10 min; the pipeline waits for th: The visitor gets the new page within minutes, old assets stay valid meanwhile
outcomes.Within 1 h through a short HTML cache, n: The visitor may see the old page for up to an hour

items.answer: Within 10 min; the pipeline waits for the invalidation, hashed assets cached long, HTML short

items.text: FR-021 leaves open whether the footer carries the company tax number (NIP). Polish e-services guides list company details among usual site disclosures. What does the footer show?
options: Legal entity plus NIP, both from the content file
Legal entity only until a legal check says NIP is required
items.recommended: Legal entity plus NIP, both from the content file
items.why: Research - Electronic Services Act finding; Brief Open decision 3; the NIP is already public in the business register
items.answer: Legal entity plus NIP, both from the content file

items.text: The Could visit counter (FR-032) would read CloudFront logs or use a privacy-first service, but research says those logs hold personal data and a hosted service would be a third-party origin (NFR-017). What becomes of it?
options: Could, after launch: CloudFront logs only, IPs minimised, short retention, privacy note updated
Wont: drop the counter so no visitor data is kept
items.recommended: Could, after launch: CloudFront logs only, IPs minimised, short retention, privacy note updated
items.why: Brief Needs (Could) 22 keeps it; Research - GDPR access-log finding sets the conditions

quotes.text: Cookieless visit counter (CloudFront logs or a privacy-first service).
CDN and web server access logs hold IP addresses and user agents, which are personal data under GDPR

items.answer: Could, after launch: CloudFront logs only, IPs minimised, short retention, privacy note updated

items.text: Jakub updates content by editing one file and merging a PR, but nothing lets him see the built page before the merge. Should a PR show it?
options: Could, not MVP: the PR check attaches the built site and screenshots at 360 px and desktop
Wont: Jakub builds and checks locally before merging
items.recommended: Could, not MVP: the PR check attaches the built site and screenshots at 360 px and desktop
items.why: Brief Users 4 implies it; implied capabilities stay out of the MVP

parts: PR check builds the site from the edited content file
Screenshots at 360 px and desktop attached to the PR
Built site downloadable as a CI artifact

hint.text: Jakub (owner) - updates content a few times a year by editing one file and merging a PR.

items.answer: Could, not MVP: the PR check attaches the built site and screenshots at 360 px and desktop

items.text: The Polish version (FR-031) is listed under Could, yet Polish translation is out of scope and English only at launch is decided. Which stands?
options: Wont for now - only the structure stays ready (NFR-024)
Could - keep it in the backlog for after launch
items.recommended: Wont for now - only the structure stays ready (NFR-024)
items.why: Brief Out of scope lists Polish translation; Constraints decide English only

quotes.text: Polish version behind a language switch.
Language: English only at launch (decided). Structure must allow a Polish version later.

items.answer: Wont for now - only the structure stays ready (NFR-024)

items.text: FR-026 stops serving the 2020 CV PDF, but old links to it are out there. What does its old URL do?
options: Redirects permanently to the new CV PDF
Returns the custom 404 page
items.recommended: Redirects permanently to the new CV PDF
items.why: FR-026 AC4 retires the 2020 PDF; old shared links should reach the current CV

steps: Someone clicks a saved link to the 2020 CV PDF
The 2020 PDF is no longer served

outcomes.Returns the custom 404 page: They see the 404 page with a link to the main page

items.answer: Redirects permanently to the new CV PDF

items.text: FR-015 publishes jakub.igla@gmail.com as a plain mailto link; research says it will be harvested, and script obfuscation breaks the no-JavaScript rule. How is the address shown?
options: Plain mailto link, accept the spam
Address shown munged in plain HTML (jakub.igla at gmail.com)
A dedicated forwarding alias instead of the personal address
items.recommended: Plain mailto link, accept the spam
items.why: Brief Decisions - Contact names this address; one-click contact matters most (Research - email harvesting finding)
items.answer: Plain mailto link, accept the spam

items.text: Two areas look not to apply: scalability (static files behind a CDN absorb a launch-post spike; cost under load sits with NFR-019) and data retention and backup (no user data; content and its history live in git). Confirm these don't apply?
options: Confirm both don't apply
One applies (name it)
items.why: Research - NFR checklist marks both likely-n/a
